ana: Ran a set of profiling runs on the 8x A100 job (tp=2, pp=1, seq=1024, bs=2). Captured nsys + nvprof + perfetto. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/trace/1772345678. Repro: recurring NCCL idle blocks around layers 18-22 (~same offsets every microbatch). Also seeing synchronous cudaMemcpyPeer right before all-reduce in the timeline. nvprof/nsys attached below.

liam: Can you paste the nvprof/gpu-trace snippet? Curious which kernels are active during the stall.

ana: Pasted a minimal nvprof GPU trace excerpt (trimmed):
```
GPU timeline (rank0):
0.000s - gemm_fwd (compute) 12ms
0.012s - mha_fused_v2 (compute) 8ms
0.020s - kv_cache_copy (cudaMemcpyPeer synchronous) 6ms
0.026s - NCCL all_reduce (ncclAllReduce) 14ms (serialized)
0.040s - softmax_generic (compute fallback) 3ms
Idle gaps ~4-6ms before next layer.
% of time spent in NCCL+memcpy ~45% in the hotspot window.
```

sasha: From that snippet it looks like kv_cache_copy is running on the default stream and blocking the compute stream, then we immediately trigger all_reduce which serializes across ranks. Two likely culprits: batching heuristic creates tight request packing (head-of-line blocking), and kernel selector picked a generic softmax for seq>512 so compute is slower and misaligned with nccl windows.

devon: Found a suspicious commit (git r/commit/abc1234) that disabled fused_softmax for attn_dim=64 on A100 due to a correctness guard; we regressed there. If fused_softmax is re-enabled for those dims the compute window shrinks and overlap improves. Also consider moving KV copy to an async stream.

ana: I ran a focused nsys capture with:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl --capture-range=process:pid=12345 -o /artifacts/nsys/1772345678
```
The NVTX markers show microbatch start/end. Perfetto flame shows NCCL all_reduce blocks sitting on the timeline matched to the same CPU thread scheduling anchor (worker-3). CPU trace shows frequent short syscalls right before the memcpy which suggests sync point on CPU.

liam: Try these quick experiments:
- enable async KV copy: move memcpy to stream 2 + `cudaMemcpyAsync` and `cudaStreamWaitEvent` on compute stream.
- set BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=2 to reduce in-flight interleaving.
- flip kernel selector to prefer `fused_softmax` for seq<=2048 on A100.
- tune NCCL: `NCCL_ALGO=Ring NCCL_BUFFSIZE=16384` (try both Ring/Tree)

ci-bot: nvprof log and nsys qdrep uploaded:
- /artifacts/nvprof/1772345678.log
- /artifacts/nsys/1772345678.qdrep
- perfetto trace: /artifacts/perfetto/1772345678.pb

sasha: Two mitigation paths imo: 1) short-term: stagger all-reduce by launching it as soon as a microbatch's KV copy completes (start earlier), and move KV memcpy to a non-blocking stream so it doesn't stall compute. 2) medium-term: adjust batching heuristic so large sequences don't force too many concurrent requests into same GPU wave, add a small jitter between microbatches to break lock-step. Also re-enable fused kernels guarded by hardware checks.

ana: I'll iterate on async memcpy + kernel selector flip + BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=2 on a canary dedicated run tomorrow morning and re-capture perfetto + nsys. Will post results. Thanks :thumbsup:
